title: Disjunction extraction from propositional Harrop assumptions

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Cut elimination (handout 5)
based_on.pages: Ch.7 §2, printed pp.3–6, cut-free intuitionistic calculus/disjunction property

summary: Extract an actual proved disjunct from a supplied intuitionistic tree whose assumptions are Harrop, retaining the chosen side and the original context.
abstract: An assumed disjunction need not give a proof of either alternative. Some assumptions nevertheless allow a proof to reveal a definite side, even when those assumptions contain disjunctions inside implication inputs. Harrop formulas describe this class. We follow the final disjunction through a supplied cut-free proof, retain the implication inputs already proved, and rebuild a factor proof with exactly the same allowed assumptions. Cut elimination extends the procedure to proofs with cuts. Discharging a Harrop assumption then gives an implication-choice result, while substitution and open-branch counterexamples explain its precise limits.
